title: add-operator-custody-escrow-and-audit-staleness-detector
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds operator custody escrow service and audit staleness detection. Admins should run migration to create escrow keyset. No user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: reduce blast radius from compromised long-lived operator credentials and detect delayed/duplicated audit streams in Private/Dedicated deployments. This PR implements an operator custody escrow service that integrates with existing per-tenant KMS providers to store short-lived operator key material under an operator-scoped CMK; it also introduces an audit staleness detector that marks and surfaces out-of-order or stale audit batches for downstream reconciliation. What changed: 1) pkg/kms/escrow.go: new escrow client and key lifecycle helpers that wrap KMS providers and implement ephemeral operator lease sealing/unsealing. 2) api/rbac/v2/policies/temporal.yaml: new RBAC v2 temporal constraints for operator leases (max-duration, geo-bound flag). 3) internal/audit/freshness_detector.go: detector logic that computes watermark per-tenant and flags batches exceeding staleness window or non-monotonic timestamps. 4) docs/security/operator-escrow.md: operational runbook and migration steps. 5) deploy/helm/templates/escrow-secret.yaml: helm hooks to provision escrow controller and optional fallback. 6) test/integration/escrow_e2e_test.go + test/unit/freshness_detector_test.go: coverage for common edge cases. Migration notes: a lightweight DB migration creates escrow_keysets table (id, tenant_id, kms_provider_hint, created_at). Operators must run `scripts/migrate_escrow_keys --create` post-deploy. Config knobs: ESCROW_MAX_LEASE_SECONDS (default 3600), AUDIT_STALENESS_THRESHOLD_SECONDS (default 300). Security considerations: escrow stored key material is encrypted with tenant CMK; controller requires role-bound service principal and is gated by new RBAC predicates. Rollout plan: staged rollout to Private and Dedicated clusters with sidecar disabled by default for Hosted. Backwards compatibility: endpoints unchanged; operator lease tokens issued by controller remain compatible, but older runtime must be restarted after migration to pick up temporal policy checks. Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] integration test added [x] docs + runbook [x] migration helper included [x] security review requested

Add RBAC v2 temporal policy for operator leases

review_comments: Miguel Hernandez: Please clarify threat model for operator key escrow and whether the escrow controller can be single-tenant by configuration.
Asha Patel: Response: the controller supports tenant isolation mode via Helm values (escrow.multiTenant=false) and will only create keys for listed tenant IDs when enabled. Added note in docs.
Sofia Liu: Can we add a metrics tag so SLOs can distinguish escrow-enforced leases versus legacy leases?
Asha Patel: Added metric 'escrow.lease_type' and a console dashboard panel in a follow-up commit.
Daniel Kim: Audit detector may produce false positives during clock skew windows; recommend a configurable tolerance and a cluster-level demotion mode.
Asha Patel: Added AUDIT_STALENESS_TOLERANCE_SECONDS and a cluster.demote_on_skew flag; updated tests to validate tolerance behavior.
